question: What is TSH (Thyroid Stimulating Hormone) and its normal lab test range?
answer:
Pituitary hormone that instructs the thyroid gland how much metabolic hormone (T3/T4) to produce. Standard Reference Range: 0.4 - 4.5 mIU/L.
- Low level: Low TSH (< 0.4 mIU/L) suggests an overactive thyroid (Hyperthyroidism). Causes weight loss, tremors, palpitations.
- High level: High TSH (> 4.5 mIU/L) signals an underactive thyroid (Hypothyroidism). Causes weight gain, hair fall, lethargy, cold intolerance.
- Dietary & Lifestyle guidance: Use iodized salt; include selenium/zinc-rich seeds (pumpkin/sunflower); limit excess raw cruciferous vegetables (cabbage, cauliflower).
